The most well-known brands include:\n\n- **Legare** (very popular, American-made, models like the 400 and 47)\n- **Creelman** (Canadian)\n- **Acme** (British)\n- **Singer** and **Scott & Williams**\n- **HBrother/Erlbacher** (German models)\n\nThey work by hand-cranking a cylinder fitted with latch hooks (needles) in a circular arrangement. You control tension, stitch count, and heel/toe shaping manually. They require a good deal of operator skill and feel.\n\n**Modern/Automated CSMs**\n\nMore recent machines like the **Erlbacher Gearhart** revivals, or fully automated versions from companies like **Sintelli** or **Kachunn** (and similar Chinese-manufactured units) can handle much of the process with motors and programmed sequences.       = 48.0      # mm \u2014 inner diameter\nCYL_H           = 75.0      # mm \u2014 total cylinder height\n\n# --- Needle slot parameters (\u26a0\ufe0f TEMPORARY \u2014 update after measurement)     = 4         # number of M5 bolts\nBOLT_D          = 5.5       # mm \u2014 bolt hole diameter (M5 clearance)\nKEY_W           = 3.0       # mm \u2014 anti-rotation key width\nKEY_H           = 3.0       # mm \u2014 key height\nKEY_L           = 15.0      # mm \u2014 key length\n\n# =============================================================================\n# CALCULATED VALUES (do not edit)\n# {CYL_ID} mm\")\nprint(f\"Cylinder Height:    {CYL_H} mm\")\nprint(f\"Needle count:       {NEEDLE_COUNT}\")\nprint(f\"Slot pitch:         {SLOT_PITCH:.3f} mm\")\nprint(f\"Slot width: angle_deg = i * (360.0 / NEEDLE_COUNT)\n    angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)\n\n    # Slot centerline at cylinder wall, radial direction\n    # Slot goes from OD inward by SLOT_DEPTH\n    slot_r_out = CYL_R_OUT + 1.0   # slight overcut at surface\n    slot_r_in  = CYL_R_OUT - SLOT_DEPTH\n\n    # Slot as a box, then rotated to correct angular position\n    # Width = SLOT_W, depth = SLOT_DEPTH, height = CYL_H - 5mm (leave bottom wall)\n    slot_h = CYL_H - 3.0  # leave 3mm floor\n\n    # Create slot as rectangular prism\n    slot_box = Part.makeBox(SLOT_W, SLOT_DEPTH + 2, slot_h)\n    # Center the slot width\n    slot_box.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-SLOT_W / 2, slot_r_in - 1, 3.0))\n\n    # Rotate to angular position\n    slot_box.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0),\n   # mm \\u2014 needle butt track width (butt width + 0.4 clearance)\\nTRACK_DEPTH     = 8.0       # mm \\u2014 needle butt track depth\\n\\n# --- Cassette interface ---\\nSHAFT_D         = 12.0      # {LOWER_ANGLE}\\u00b0\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"Needle track width: {TRACK_W} mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"Needle track depth: {TRACK_DEPTH} mm\\\")\\nprint(\\\"=\\\" * 60)\\nprint(\\\"FITS Anycubic Kobra 2: YES Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead:\n- Group nodes by **category** \u2014 all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal.\n- For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** \u2014 warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert.\n- Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps).\n- Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp.\n- **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept \u2014 those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.)\n\n**Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --color-text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** \u2014 title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds.\n\n**Light/dark mode quick pick** \u2014 use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values:\n- **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle**\n- **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle**\n- Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` \u2014 paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke=\"#...\"` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink.\n\nFor status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps.\n\n\n\n## Charts (Chart.js)\n```html\n<div style=\"position: relative; width: 100%; height: 300px;\">\n  <canvas id=\"myChart\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Bar chart of quarterly revenue, Q1 through Q4\">Quarterly revenue: Q1 12, Q2 19, Q3 8, Q4 15.</canvas>\n</div>\n<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/Chart.js/4.4.1/chart.umd.js\"></script>\n<script>\n  new Chart(document.getElementById('myChart'), {\n    type: 'bar',\n    data: { labels: ['Q1','Q2','Q3','Q4'], datasets: [{ label: 'Revenue', data: [12,19,8,15] }] },\n    options: { responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false }\n  });\n</script>\n```\n\n**Chart.js rules**:\n- Every `<canvas>` MUST have `role=\"img\"` and a descriptive `aria-label` summarizing what the chart shows, plus fallback text between the tags. Without these the chart is invisible to screen readers.\n- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series. Pair each color with a secondary visual cue \u2014 dash pattern for lines, marker shape for scatter, fill pattern/hatching for bars and pie slices \u2014 and show both color and cue in the legend.\n- Canvas cannot resolve CSS variables. Use hardcoded hex or Chart.js defaults.\n- Wrap `<canvas>` in `<div>` with explicit `height` and `position: relative`.\n- **Canvas sizing**: set height ONLY on the wrapper div, never on the canvas element itself. Use position: relative on the wrapper and responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false in Chart.js options. Never set CSS height directly on canvas \u2014 this causes wrong dimensions, especially for horizontal bar charts.\n- For horizontal bar charts: wrapper div height should be at least (number_of_bars * 40) + 80 pixels.\n- Load UMD build via `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` \u2014 sets `window.Chart` global. Follow with plain `<script>` (no `type=\"module\"`).\n- Multiple charts: use unique IDs (`myChart1`, `myChart2`). Each gets its own canvas+div pair.\n- For bubble and scatter charts: bubble radii extend past their center points, so points near axis boundaries get clipped. Pad the scale range \u2014 set `scales.y.min` and `scales.y.max` ~10% beyond your data range (same for x). Or use `layout: { padding: 20 }` as a blunt fallback.\n- Chart.js auto-skips x-axis labels when they'd overlap. If you have \u226412 categories and need all labels visible (waterfall, monthly series), set `scales.x.ticks: { autoSkip: false, maxRotation: 45 }` \u2014 missing labels make bars unidentifiable.\n\n**Number formatting**: negative values are `-$5M` not `$-5M` \u2014 sign before currency symbol. Use a formatter: `(v) => (v < 0 ? '-' : '') + '$' + Math.abs(v) + 'M'`.\n\n**Legends** \u2014 always disable Chart.js default and build custom HTML. The default uses round dots and no values; custom HTML gives small squares, tight spacing, and percentages:\n\n```js\nplugins: { legend: { display: false } }\n```\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 8px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);\">\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #3266ad;\"></span>Chrome 65%</span>\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #73726c;\"></span>Safari 18%</span>\n</div>\n```\n\nInclude the value/percentage in each label when the data is categorical (pie, donut, single-series bar). Position the legend above the chart (`margin-bottom`) or below (`margin-top`) \u2014 not inside the canvas.\n\n**Dashboard layout** \u2014 wrap summary numbers in metric cards (see UI fragment) above the chart. Chart canvas flows below without a card wrapper. Use `sendPrompt()` for drill-down: `sendPrompt('Break down Q4 by region')`.\n\n## Geographic maps (D3 choropleth)\n\n**Never invent coordinates** \u2014 no hand-drawn SVG paths, no inline GeoJSON. Fetch real topology or don't draw a map.\n\nThree topology sources on jsdelivr. CSP only allows `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com` \u2014 do NOT try `raw.githubusercontent.com` or other hosts, the fetch will silently fail. Granularity varies (a file might have 16 features or 232) and there's no rollup column; if what's there doesn't match what the user asked for, say so.\n\n```html\n<div id=\"map\" style=\"width: 100%;\"></div>\n<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/d3/7.8.5/d3.min.js\"></script>\n<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/topojson/3.0.2/topojson.min.js\"></script>\n<script>\nconst values = { 'California': 39, 'Texas': 30, 'New York': 19 /* ...keyed on what you saw in web_fetch */ };\nconst isDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;\nconst color = d3.scaleQuantize([0, 40], isDark ? d3.schemeBlues[5].slice().reverse() : d3.schemeBlues[5]);\nconst svg = d3.select('#map').append('svg').attr('viewBox', '0 0 900 560').attr('width', '100%');\nconst path = d3.geoPath(d3.geoAlbersUsa().scale(1100).translate([450, 280]));\nd3.json('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/states-10m.json').then(us => {\n  svg.selectAll('path').data(topojson.feature(us, us.objects.states).features).join('path')\n    .attr('d', path).attr('stroke', isDark ? Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead:\n- Group nodes by **category** \u2014 all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal.\n- For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** \u2014 warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert.\n- Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps).\n- Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp.\n- **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept \u2014 those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.)\n\n**Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --color-text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** \u2014 title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds.\n\n**Light/dark mode quick pick** \u2014 use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values:\n- **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle**\n- **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle**\n- Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` \u2014 paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke=\"#...\"` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink.\n\nFor status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. Without these the chart is invisible to screen readers.\n- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series. Pair each color with a secondary visual cue \u2014 dash pattern for lines, marker shape for scatter, fill pattern/hatching for bars and pie slices \u2014 and show both color and cue in the legend.\n- Canvas cannot resolve CSS variables. Use hardcoded hex or Chart.js defaults.\n- Wrap `<canvas>` in `<div>` with explicit `height` and `position: relative`.\n- **Canvas sizing**: set height ONLY on the wrapper div, never on the canvas element itself. Use position: relative on the wrapper and responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false in Chart.js options. Never set CSS height directly on canvas \u2014 this causes wrong dimensions, especially for horizontal bar charts.\n- For horizontal bar charts: wrapper div height should be at least (number_of_bars * 40) + 80 pixels.\n- Load UMD build via `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` \u2014 sets `window.Chart` global. Follow with plain `<script>` (no `type=\"module\"`).\n- Multiple charts: use unique IDs (`myChart1`, `myChart2`). Each gets its own canvas+div pair.\n- For bubble and scatter charts: bubble radii extend past their center points, so points near axis boundaries get clipped. Pad the scale range \u2014 set `scales.y.min` and `scales.y.max` ~10% beyond your data range (same for x). Or use `layout: { padding: 20 }` as a blunt fallback.\n- Chart.js auto-skips x-axis labels when they'd overlap. If you have \u226412 categories and need all labels visible (waterfall, monthly series), set `scales.x.ticks: { autoSkip: false, maxRotation: 45 }` \u2014 missing labels make bars unidentifiable.\n\n**Number formatting**: negative values are `-$5M` not `$-5M` \u2014 sign before currency symbol. Use a formatter: `(v) => (v < 0 ? '-' : '') + '$' + Math.abs(v) + 'M'`.\n\n**Legends** \u2014 always disable Chart.js default and build custom HTML. The default uses round dots and no values; custom HTML gives small squares, tight spacing, and percentages:\n\n```js\nplugins: { legend: { display: false } }\n```\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 8px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);\">\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #3266ad;\"></span>Chrome 65%</span>\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #73726c;\"></span>Safari 18%</span>\n</div>\n```\n\nInclude the value/percentage in each label when the data is categorical (pie, donut, single-series bar). Position the legend above the chart (`margin-bottom`) or below (`margin-top`) \u2014 not inside the canvas.\n\n**Dashboard layout** \u2014 wrap summary numbers in metric cards (see UI fragment) above the chart. Chart canvas flows below without a card wrapper. Use `sendPrompt()` for drill-down: `sendPrompt('Break down Q4 by region')`.\n\n## Geographic maps (D3 choropleth)\n\n**Never invent coordinates** \u2014 no hand-drawn SVG paths, no inline GeoJSON. matches cylinder + cam ring\\n    angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)\\n    px = PIN_R * math.cos(angle_rad)\\n    py = PIN_R * math.sin(angle_rad)\\n    # Through hole (H7 fit: +0.0/+0.025mm tolerance)\\n    pin_hole = Part.makeCylinder(PIN_D/2 + 0.01, BASE_H + BOSS_H + 2)\\n    pin_hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(px, py, -1))\\n    base_body = base_body.cut(pin_hole)\\n    print(f\\\"  Pin hole {i+1}: ({px:.1f}, {py:.1f})\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# CASSETTE CLAMP BOLT HOLES (M5, heat inserts on TOP face)\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(BOLT_COUNT):\\n    angle_deg = i * 90.0 + 45.0\\n    angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)\\n    bx = BOLT_R * math.cos(angle_rad)\\n    by = BOLT_R * math.sin(angle_rad)\\n    # M5 heat insert hole (6.4mm OD, 8mm deep from top)\\n    insert = Part.makeCylinder(INSERT_D/2, 8.0)\\n    insert.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, BASE_H + BOSS_H - 8.0))\\n    base_body = base_body.cut(insert)\\n    # Clearance through bottom\\n    clr = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_D/2, BASE_H + BOSS_H + 2)\\n    clr.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\\n    base_body = base_body.cut(clr)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# SHAFT COLLAR BOLT HOLES (3\\u00d7 M4, lock base to shaft collar)\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(COLLAR_COUNT):\\n    angle_deg = i * 120.0\\n    angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)\\n    cx = COLLAR_R * math.cos(angle_rad)\\n    cy = COLLAR_R * math.sin(angle_rad)\\n    collar_hole = Part.makeCylinder(COLLAR_D/2, BASE_H + 2)\\n    collar_hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(cx, cy, -1))\\n    base_body = base_body.cut(collar_hole)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# ANTI-ROTATION KEY SLOT (on boss, matches cylinder key)\\n# =============================================================================\\nkey_slot = Part.makeBox(KEY_W + 0.1, KEY_W + 0.1, BOSS_H + 2)\\nkey_slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-(KEY_W+0.1)/2, BOSS_R - KEY_W - 0.5,\\n                                   BASE_H - 1))\\nbase_body = base_body.cut(key_slot)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# RADIAL STABILIZER PADS (3\\u00d7, help center cylinder on boss)\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(PAD_COUNT):\\n    angle_deg = i * 120.0 + 60.0   # between pin positions\\n    pad = Part.makeBox(PAD_W, PAD_DEPTH, PAD_H)\\n    pad.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-PAD_W/2, BOSS_R - 0.5, BASE_H))\\n    pad.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), angle_deg)\\n    base_body = base_body.fuse(pad)\\n\\n# Weight relief pockets (reduce mass, keep stiffness)\\nfor i in range(6):\\n    angle_deg = i * 60.0\\n    angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)\\n    px = 55.0 * math.cos(angle_rad)\\n    py = 55.0 * math.sin(angle_rad)\\n    pocket = Part.makeCylinder(12.0, BASE_H - 3)\\n    pocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(px, py, 1.5))\\n    base_body = base_body.cut(pocket)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# FINALIZE\\n# =============================================================================\\nobj = doc.addObject(\\\"Part::Feature\\\", \\\"CSM_CassetteBase_OD150\\\")\\nobj.Shape = base_body\\nobj.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.45, 0.50, 0.55)\\ndoc.recompute()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.activeDocument().activeView().viewIsometric()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.SendMsgToActiveView(\\\"ViewFit\\\")\\n\\nvol = base_body.Volume\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n\\u2705 Cassette base plate complete\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Volume: {vol:.0f} mm\\u00b3  Weight: {vol*1.27/1000:.1f}g\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n\\ud83d\\udccb PRINT SETTINGS:\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Material: PETG + M5 brass heat inserts (\\u00d74)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Layer: 0.15mm | Perimeters: 4 | Top/Bottom: 5 solid\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Infill: 60% Gyroid | Orientation: FLAT\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Fits bed: YES ({BASE_OD}mm < 220mm)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n\\ud83d\\udd29 HARDWARE:\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   4\\u00d7 M5 brass heat inserts (install with soldering iron, 200\\u00b0C)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   3\\u00d7 \\u00d84mm \\u00d7 16mm hardened steel dowel pins\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   3\\u00d7 M4\\u00d710mm socket bolts (collar to shaft)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n\\ud83d\\udd29 ASSEMBLY ORDER:\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   1. Heat-set M5 inserts into bolt holes (top face)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   2. Press \\u00d84mm dowel pins into pin holes (from bottom)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   3. Slide base onto 12mm shaft\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   4. Install shaft collar + M4 bolts (lock axially)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   5. Drop cylinder over dowel pins (pins into cylinder blind holes)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   6. Drop cam ring over same dowel pins\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   7. Torque M5 cassette clamp bolts to 1.5 Nm\\\")\\n\\nimport os\\nout = os.path.expanduser(\\n    \\\"~/CSM_PROJECT/01_MECHANICAL/02_CASSETTE_HEAD/\\\")\\nPart.export([obj], out + \\\"assembly/CSM_V3_CassetteBase_OD150.stl\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n\\ud83d\\udcbe STL saved\\\")\\n\", \"filename\": \"/mnt/user-data/outputs/3D-PROJECT/01_MECHANICAL/02_CASSETTE_HEAD/cassette_base/CSM_V3_CassetteBase.FCMacro\"}"
